title: A quasi-compact relative diagonal descends along a gerbe
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use algebraic stacks [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and morphisms and $2$-fibre products of fibred groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Quasi-compactness is [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism], and point spaces have the topology of [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. A morphism $p:\mathcal U\to Q$ to an algebraic space is a gerbe if for every scheme $T\to Q$ its fibre groupoid has objects fppf locally on $T$, and any two objects of that fibre groupoid are isomorphic fppf locally on $T$ [def-pc-fppf-site]. Let $p:\mathcal U\to Q$ be a gerbe, with $\mathcal U$ an algebraic stack and $Q$ an algebraic space over $S$. If $\Delta_{\mathcal U/S}:\mathcal U\to\mathcal U\times_S\mathcal U$ is quasi-compact, then $\Delta_{Q/S}:Q\to Q\times_SQ$ is quasi-compact. In particular $Q$ is quasi-separated relative to $S$, meaning that every scheme test of this diagonal is a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces. There is no quasi-compactness assumption on $\mathcal U$, $Q$ or $S$, and no separatedness, finite-type or Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0DQL (lemma-gerbe-diagonal-quasi-compact), relative over the common base scheme S.

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $u:V\to\mathcal U$. The atlas clause of [lem-sfb-gerbe-smooth-universal-homeomorphism] says that $h=pu:V\to Q$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Put $B=V\times_SV$, $D=Q\times_SQ$, $R=V\times_{\mathcal U}V$ and $W=V\times_QV$. The scheme $B$ exists by [def-pc-fibre-product], and $D,W$ are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The space-source representability theorem [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability], applied to $V\to\mathcal U$, makes $R$ an algebraic space. All these objects are over the original $S$; no absolute diagonal over a different base is substituted.

source.place: Tag 0DQL (lemma-gerbe-diagonal-quasi-compact), diagram; Tag 06QI (lemma-gerbe-fppf), after choosing an atlas.

proof.text: The morphism $R\to B$ is the base change of $\Delta_{\mathcal U/S}$ along $u\times_Su:B\to\mathcal U\times_S\mathcal U$. Indeed a section of $R$ is a pair $(v_1,v_2)$ together with an isomorphism $u(v_1)\simeq u(v_2)$, which is precisely the diagonal pullback; eliminating the repeated object gives inverse functors on the defining triples. The product $\mathcal U\times_S\mathcal U$ is an algebraic stack by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products] (the scheme $S$ viewed as the final algebraic stack), so $\Delta_{\mathcal U/S}$ is a morphism of algebraic stacks; it is representable by algebraic spaces by the algebraic-stack definition. Its assumed quasi-compactness, and the equivalence of scheme and stack tests in [lem-sfb-representable-stack-quasicompact-tests], therefore imply that $R\to B$ is quasi-compact as a morphism of algebraic spaces. Forgetting the displayed isomorphism defines $r:R\to W$, since applying $p$ to it gives equality in the discrete groupoid $Q$. Its composite with $W\to B$ is the preceding map.

source.place: Tag 0DQL, top horizontal composite and cartesian diagonal test; Tag 050T (lemma-characterize-representable-quasi-compact).

proof.text: For every affine scheme $T\to B$, write $R_T=R\times_BT$ and $W_T=W\times_BT$. The map $|R_T|\to|W_T|$ is surjective: a field-valued section of $W_T$ consists of the fixed $T$-section and two $V$-sections whose images in $Q$ coincide. Their images in $\mathcal U$ are consequently two objects of the same gerbe fibre. By the gerbe hypothesis they are isomorphic on an fppf cover of that field spectrum. Some member of this jointly surjective cover is nonempty; taking the residue field at any of its points gives a field extension and the required isomorphism, hence a point of $R_T$ mapping to the given point class. The $V$-sections and $T$-section are kept fixed under extension. This is the elementary local-isomorphism clause in the definition of a gerbe, not a claim that $r$ is smooth or quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0DQL, surjectivity of the top left arrow, checked after the atlas and arbitrary affine base change; Tag 0CPS (proposition-when-gerbe-over), local-isomorphism direction.

proof.text: The quasi-compactness of $R\to B$ gives quasi-compactness of $R_T$ for each affine $T\to B$, by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. The space and topological predicates agree by the last sentence of [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. The map $|R_T|\to|W_T|$ is continuous by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] and surjective by step 3. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact]: its image is all of $|W_T|$, so that space is quasi-compact. The same atlas/topology equivalence makes $W_T$ quasi-compact as an algebraic space. The affine-test equivalence of [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests] now gives quasi-compactness of $W\to B$. This is quasi-compactness for quasi-compact scheme tests; for a quasi-compact space $Z\to B$ with a surjective etale map $Z'\to Z$ from a quasi-compact scheme, $W\times_BZ'$ is quasi-compact and $W\times_BZ'\to W\times_BZ$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], so $|W\times_BZ|$ is a continuous image of a quasi-compact space and $W\times_BZ$ is quasi-compact by the same three point-topology nodes. Thus $W\to B$ is quasi-compact in the space-test sense of [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local] used in step 6. This is the atlas form of the surjective-image argument in Tag 050X; it assumes no quasi-compactness of the atlas $V$ itself.

source.place: Tag 0DQL, application of Tag 050X (lemma-surjection-from-quasi-compact); topology.tex Tag 04Z9 (lemma-image-quasi-compact).

proof.text: The map $b=h\times_Sh:B\to D$ factors as $V\times_SV\to V\times_SQ\to Q\times_SQ$. The first arrow is the base change of $h$ along $V\times_SQ\to Q$ (second projection), and the second is the base change of $h$ along $Q\times_SQ\to Q$ (first projection). The base-change and composition laws of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] show that $b$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. These laws are applied to morphisms of algebraic spaces, thus representable by algebraic spaces; representability can also be read from [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability] with the target a discrete algebraic-space stack. No quasi-compactness is required of $h$ or $b$.

source.place: Tag 0DQL, right vertical arrow; Tags 06PX (lemma-composition-flat), 06PY (lemma-base-change-flat), 06Q3 (lemma-composition-finite-presentation), 06Q4 (lemma-base-change-finite-presentation); stacks-properties.tex Tags 04ZT, 04ZU for surjectivity.

proof.text: The square with horizontal maps $W\to B$ and $\Delta_{Q/S}:Q\to D$ is cartesian. On sections, $B\times_DQ$ consists of $(v_1,v_2,q)$ with $h(v_1)=q=h(v_2)$; deleting $q$ gives $W$ and reinserting their common value is the inverse. Thus $W\to B$ is the base change of $\Delta_{Q/S}$ by the surjective flat locally finitely presented map $b$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local] to the singleton family $\{b:B\to D\}$: step 4 supplies the quasi-compact base change, and step 5 supplies every covering hypothesis. Hence $\Delta_{Q/S}$ is quasi-compact. By [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism] this says that $Q/S$ is quasi-separated. The base-change clause of the fppf-locality node also gives quasi-compactness on every scheme test of the diagonal. This proves all the conclusions over the original base without additional finiteness or separation assumptions.

source.place: Tag 0DQL, final descent; spaces-descent.tex Tag 041L (lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact), using an algebraic-space atlas in place of stack descent Tag 0DQK.
